scenes.tts: How do you find the genes for a death, when you do not know which proteins are involved?
scenes.visual: Title card: Cells Marked with an X. Question card below it.
scenes.narration: How do you find the genes for a death, when you do not know which proteins are involved?

scenes.tts: The worm see elegans is about a millimetre long, and it is transparent.
scenes.caption: The worm C. elegans is about a millimetre long, and it is transparent.
scenes.visual: Worm with a 1 mm scale bar. Label: C. elegans.
scenes.narration: The worm C. elegans is about a millimetre long, and it is transparent.

scenes.tts: With Nomarski optics, its nuclei are visible in the living animal, without any staining.
scenes.visual: Nuclei stand out in relief inside the living worm. Label: Nomarski optics, no stain.
scenes.narration: With Nomarski optics, its nuclei are visible in the living animal, without any staining.

scenes.tts: Researchers followed its cells as they divided, and drew the full family tree.
scenes.visual: A lineage tree grows downward, branch by branch.
scenes.narration: Researchers followed its cells as they divided, and drew the full family tree.

scenes.tts: Some branches end in a death. On the chart, each death is marked with an X.
scenes.visual: Several branch tips receive an X.
scenes.narration: Some branches end in a death. On the chart, each death is marked with an X.

scenes.tts: The same identified cells die in every animal, at the same place in the tree.
scenes.visual: Three worms' trees side by side; the Xs line up exactly.
scenes.narration: The same identified cells die in every animal, at the same place in the tree.

scenes.tts: Counting both lineages, one hundred thirty-one of the hermaphrodite's one thousand ninety somatic cells die during development.
scenes.visual: On screen: 131 of 1,090 somatic cells die (hermaphrodite, embryonic plus postembryonic lineages).
scenes.narration: Counting both lineages, 131 of the hermaphrodite's 1,090 somatic cells die during development.
scenes.caption: Counting both lineages, 131 of the hermaphrodite's 1,090 somatic cells die during development.

scenes.tts: A death that happens to a named cell, on schedule, is a phenotype. And a phenotype can be screened for.
scenes.visual: One X highlighted with the label: a phenotype.
scenes.narration: A death that happens to a named cell, on schedule, is a phenotype. And a phenotype can be screened for.

scenes.tts: Horvitz's laboratory started from a mutant called ced-one. In it, corpses are not engulfed, so they stay visible.
scenes.caption: Horvitz's laboratory started from a mutant called ced-1. In it, corpses are not engulfed, so they stay visible.
scenes.visual: Worm with glowing, lingering corpses. Label: ced-1, corpses stay visible.
scenes.narration: Horvitz's laboratory started from a mutant called ced-1. In it, corpses are not engulfed, so they stay visible.

scenes.tts: They searched for new mutations in which the corpses never appeared.
scenes.visual: Many worms screened; in one, the glowing corpses are missing.
scenes.narration: They searched for new mutations in which the corpses never appeared.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-six they reported two genes, ced-three and ced-four.
scenes.caption: In 1986 they reported two genes, ced-3 and ced-4.
scenes.visual: Credit: 1986. Two gene labels: ced-3, ced-4.
scenes.narration: In 1986 they reported two genes, ced-3 and ced-4.

scenes.tts: In strong mutants, the cells that should have died lived. Some took on features of neurons.
scenes.visual: The X cells survive and grow small neurites.
scenes.narration: In strong mutants, the cells that should have died lived. Some took on features of neurons.

scenes.tts: Then came a gene that works the other way. It is called ced-nine.
scenes.caption: Then came a gene that works the other way. It is called ced-9.
scenes.visual: A third gene label: ced-9.
scenes.narration: Then came a gene that works the other way. It is called ced-9.

scenes.tts: A gain-of-function mutation in ced-nine kept doomed cells alive.
scenes.caption: A gain-of-function mutation in ced-9 kept doomed cells alive.
scenes.visual: Gain of function in ced-9: X cells survive.
scenes.narration: A gain-of-function mutation in ced-9 kept doomed cells alive.

scenes.tts: Loss of ced-nine killed cells that should have lived. With severe loss of ced-nine, the worms die as embryos.
scenes.caption: Loss of ced-9 killed cells that should have lived. With severe loss of ced-9, the worms die as embryos.
scenes.visual: Loss of ced-9: extra Xs appear on branches that normally live.
scenes.narration: Loss of ced-9 killed cells that should have lived. With severe loss of ced-9, the worms die as embryos.

scenes.tts: Put the results in a table, one genotype per row. Losing ced-three or ced-four saves doomed cells. Losing ced-nine kills extra cells.
scenes.visual: Genotype table builds row by row: wild type; loss of ced-3 or ced-4; gain of ced-9; loss of ced-9. Columns: cells that normally die, cells that normally live.
scenes.narration: Put the results in a table, one genotype per row. Losing ced-3 or ced-4 saves doomed cells. Losing ced-9 kills extra cells.
scenes.caption: Put the results in a table, one genotype per row. Losing ced-3 or ced-4 saves doomed cells. Losing ced-9 kills extra cells.

scenes.tts: Now remove both ced-nine and ced-three. Do the extra deaths still happen?
scenes.caption: Now remove both ced-9 and ced-3. Do the extra deaths still happen?
scenes.visual: Last row: loss of ced-9 and ced-3, with two question marks.
scenes.narration: Now remove both ced-9 and ced-3. Do the extra deaths still happen?

scenes.tts: No. Few cells die, and the embryos survive.
scenes.visual: The question marks become 'live' and 'live'.
scenes.narration: No. Few cells die, and the embryos survive.

scenes.tts: Removing ced-four instead of ced-three gives the same result.
scenes.caption: Removing ced-4 instead of ced-3 gives the same result.
scenes.visual: A note under the row: same with ced-9 plus ced-4.
scenes.narration: Removing ced-4 instead of ced-3 gives the same result.

scenes.tts: If removing the killer cancels the effect of removing the brake, the brake works through the killer.
scenes.visual: Rule card fills: remove the killer, cancel the brake's loss, so the brake works through the killer.
scenes.narration: If removing the killer cancels the effect of removing the brake, the brake works through the killer.

scenes.tts: So, in genetic order, ced-nine acts upstream. It is a brake on the two killers.
scenes.caption: So, in genetic order, CED-9 acts upstream. It is a brake on the two killers.
scenes.visual: Arrow diagram: CED-9 brake bar on CED-4 and CED-3.
scenes.narration: So, in genetic order, CED-9 acts upstream. It is a brake on the two killers.

scenes.tts: Genetic order does not, by itself, show which proteins touch.
scenes.visual: Small caveat note under the diagram: genetic order, not contact.
scenes.narration: Genetic order does not, by itself, show which proteins touch.

scenes.tts: One more gene sits above the brake. It is called E G L one.
scenes.caption: One more gene sits above the brake. It is called EGL-1.
scenes.visual: EGL-1 appears above CED-9.
scenes.narration: One more gene sits above the brake. It is called EGL-1.

scenes.tts: E G L one carries only a short stretch, called a B H three domain.
scenes.caption: EGL-1 carries only a short stretch, called a BH3 domain.
scenes.visual: EGL-1 drawn as a short protein with one marked segment. Label: BH3 domain.
scenes.narration: EGL-1 carries only a short stretch, called a BH3 domain.

scenes.tts: It binds ced-nine and releases the brake.
scenes.caption: It binds CED-9 and releases the brake.
scenes.visual: EGL-1 binds CED-9; the brake bar lifts off CED-4 and CED-3.
scenes.narration: It binds CED-9 and releases the brake.

scenes.tts: It is needed for most somatic cell deaths in the worm. Without it, most doomed cells live.
scenes.visual: Card beside the table: without EGL-1, most doomed cells live.
scenes.narration: It is needed for most somatic cell deaths in the worm. Without it, most doomed cells live.

scenes.tts: So the worm's core pathway has one brake. Ced-nine holds back the killers, and E G L one releases it.
scenes.caption: So the worm's core pathway has one brake. CED-9 holds back the killers, and EGL-1 releases it.
scenes.visual: End card line: in the core worm pathway, one brake. CED-9 holds the killers; EGL-1 releases it.
scenes.narration: So the worm's core pathway has one brake. CED-9 holds back the killers, and EGL-1 releases it.
